newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Jan 10.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Jan 10.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian cricket selectors chairman Trevor Hohns said yesterday Australian captain Mark Taylor's position in the team was not in danger. Hohns said Taylor, who is not holding his position as a batsman but is widely regarded as one of the best Test captains Australia has had, has the full support of the selectors, who are happy to see him playing in Perth against the West Indies this Sunday. Page 22.

Australian golfer Ian Baker-Finch returned to the circuit after six months off in the Victorian Open at the Victorian Golf Club. Crowds were not disappointed, as Baker-Finch, who won the 1991 British Open, but has made only one halfway cut in the past 2-1/2 years, produced some magnificent short play. Page 22.

Victorian Jockeys' Association president Neville Watson said the VJA has voted unanimously to affiliate with the Australian Workers' Union, which has appointed a negotiator to argue its case for higher riding fees. The VJA last night cancelled a planned eeting with the VRC administrators last night. Page 22.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Former Australian cricket captain Kim Hughes last night blamed Australian selectors for captain Mark Taylor's form slump, saying the dropping of Michael Slater broke up a successful opening partnership. Hughes also blames the media for placing extra presure on Taylor. Page 36.

The last two remaining Australians in the Sydney International, Pat Rafter and Sandon Stolle, lost their quarter final matches yesterday, further diminishing the prospect of seeing an Australian hold the trophy at the Australian Open. Australian tennis stocks are weak this year due to injury and a lack of form, match practice and confidence. Page 36.

The New South Wales Sheffield Shield cricket team fell to all out for 126 in their match against Western Australia at the Sydney Cricket Ground. The West Australians stand now at 8/180, on a lushly garnished wicket that for the day saw 18 wickets fall fo 306 runs. Page 35.
THE AGE

The organisers of the Ford Australian Open will avoid the problems encountered at last year's US Open by sticking with the world rankings for the seedings of this year's tournament. Pete Sampras and Steffi Graf are the top seeds for the tournament, with defending men's champion Boris Becker coming in at No. 6. Page C8.

Officials from the Monash, Greater Dandenong and Casey Councils have met with executives from the St Kilda and Hawthorn AFL clubs, the co-tenants of Waverley Park, to lobby them to retain Waverley Park, whose future is threatened by the proposed Docklands Stadium. Page C6.

Australian soccer coach Terry Venables has, on the advice of his assistant coach, replaced Collingwood Warriors flanker Goran Lozanovski and Sydney United centre-back Tony Popovic with Robert Trajkovski and Luke Casserly, after Lozanovski and Popovic withrew from the Socceroos' four nation tournament against South Korea, New Zealand and Norway. Page C6.
THE HERALD SUN

West Australian golfer Stephen Leaney yesterday made a spectacular start to his defence of the Victorian Open by hitting a course record eight under of 64. He leads New Zealander Paul Devenport by two shots and his round included six birdies, an eagle two at the first, and 11 pars. Page 106.

The Australian Drug Sports Agency has compiled its 1995 international drug testing statistics, finding that Australia's elite athletes return one of the lowest rates of positive drug tests in the world. The survey began three years ago in response to Ausralian athlete concerns over little drug testing in Australia. Page 104.

The second round of the Skilled Bay Cycling Classic saw Queenslander Rob McEwen, arguably one of the world's fastest sprinters, show he is a much stronger rider after a tough initiation into the international circuit last year. In his second win of the sries, McEwen showed smart tactics, not making his move until three quarters of the way through the race. Page 103.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The Australian Jockey Committee will today hear the collective case of 19 New South Wales jockeys, appealing against total fines of A$26,300 after last weekend's strike. A waive of the fines would be seen as a conciliatory step by the AJC, who met yeserday with a delegation of New South Wales jockeys, including Darren Beadman and Shane Dye. Page 112.

In her first Melbourne press conference for three years, world No. 1 women's tennis player Steffi Graf said it is not her goal to win four Grand Slam events this year as she did in 1988 - rather than set goals, Graf works on challenges, enjoyment and motiation. Graf has missed the Australian Open for the past two years. Page 110.

Australian rugby union player Willie Ofahengaue has shed 12 kilograms from his mighty frame, and Wallaby colleague Phil Kearns has found a cure for his Achilles tendon problem that looked to end his career. Both players have not represented Australia since the 1995 Bledisloe Cup series. Page 107.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
